approach: Add `athena_gate::attribution::check_attribution(git, main_tip, now)`. It reads only athena/records: landing-intents/ and landings/ via `ls_tree_under` plus `cat_blobs`, parsed with `HistoryRecord::parse`. It also audits the records branch's own history (a new helper in athena-git `records_branch.rs`). It walks `rev-list --first-parent --parents <main_tip>` oldest first, starting at the earliest intent's `expected_base`. The start commit is the base itself (it is the commit the intent expects as its base). For each commit: attributed if a landing names it as host_commit and the intent that landing cites (`landing.intent`) has `matches(tree, first parent)`. If it is not attributed, it is pending when some matching intent exists and now is within 15 minutes of `created_at`. Anything else is a finding: the matching intent has gone stale, or the commit is unattributed. The check time `now` is a parameter, so tests control it. A missing ref, no intent, or a first-intent base off main's line is a finding, not silent success. The CLI adds `check --attribution` (conflicts with --history and --pr-head), prints a report, and exits 2 on any finding. CI gets a non-blocking `attribution` job that fetches athena/records first.

decisions.choice: Take the time as a `jiff::Timestamp` argument; the CLI passes `Timestamp::now()`.
decisions.reason: Tests can then set the 15-minute window exactly, without sleeping.

rejected.option: Read the clock inside the check
rejected.why: Tests could not pin the window and would be flaky.

decisions.choice: Judge a landing's head tree and expected base through the intent the landing cites (`landing.intent`), using `LandingIntent::matches(tree, parent)`.
decisions.reason: The Landing record has no tree field; its intent holds head_tree_sha and expected_base. Reusing `matches` keeps one definition, shared with reconcile.

rejected.why: That is the PR's commits, not the head tree the intent announced; it would not check the expected base.

decisions.choice: Read the records ref as local refs/heads/athena/records first, then refs/remotes/origin/athena/records. Report a finding if both exist and neither is an ancestor of the other.
decisions.reason: The CI fetch makes the local ref exist; a developer checkout may only have the remote-tracking one. This also catches a rewritten (force-pushed) remote.

rejected.why: Contradicts the brief's `git fetch origin athena/records:athena/records`.

decisions.choice: Define "not a fast-forward" in a new `records_branch` helper `audit_history(git, tip)`. Walk the first-parent chain from the tip. Report a commit that is a second root (no parent mid-chain, or a different root than expected) and a commit whose tree drops or changes any file its first parent held (append-only broken). Extra parents (landing commits carry the PR head, §6.1) are allowed.
decisions.reason: A snapshot cannot show a past force-push, but it does show a rewritten history by these two symptoms. Landing commits' extra parents rule out a 'single parent' test.

rejected.option: Require every commit to have exactly one parent
rejected.why: Landing commits legitimately have a second parent (append_to_remote extra_parents).

decisions.choice: Use the main tip "HEAD" (as `check --history` does), and list the walk's start commit among those judged.
decisions.reason: CI checks out the pushed sha or the default branch. The base is the commit the first intent expects, so the check covers it and not older commits.

rejected.option: Skip the base commit like reconcile does (start = base + 1)
rejected.why: The request says walk from the base onward, so the base is judged.

decisions.choice: Do not parse commit trailers or call the host.
decisions.reason: Criterion 6 forbids trailers; the check is records-only.

files.purpose: `check_attribution`, `AttributionReport` and `Finding`, with doc comments citing records-history.md §5.2, §6, §10 and D111. Includes the unit tests for criteria 1 to 4 and the pre-base test.
Add a reader for the records ref (local, else remote-tracking, with a divergence report) and `audit_history`. Both are read-only and tested.
Only if needed: expose a small shared first-parent listing helper. Otherwise leave it untouched. The check itself does not change.

Add the `--attribution` flag on Check (conflicts with history and pr_head, as `--pr-head` already conflicts with `--history`). Dispatch to the check, print text or JSON, exit 2 on a finding. Update the help doc.
`attribution_report` renderer that names each unattributed or expired commit.
Tests for the help listing, the flag conflicts, and a failing exit with no records branch.
Add the non-blocking `attribution` job beside `history`. Governance file, a listed deliverable.
Entry for `athena check --attribution`, following the file's existing format.

steps: Read docs/design/records-history.md §5.2, §6, §10 and D111 to confirm the 15-minute pending rule and the non-fast-forward wording.
In records_branch.rs, add the ref reader (local then origin remote-tracking, with a divergence note) and `audit_history`, with unit tests.

Create attribution.rs: load intents and landings (dirs `landing-intents` and `landings`) at the records tip with `ls_tree_under` and `cat_blobs`, then `HistoryRecord::parse`. A record that fails to parse becomes a finding. Take the earliest intent by (created_at, id), as reconcile does. Walk `rev-list --first-parent --parents`, reversed, from its `expected_base`. For each commit apply the attributed, pending, stale and unattributed rules. Skip commits before the base.
Add the unit tests: pass, unrecorded, pending boundary (+14, +15, +16 minutes), a landing whose intent does not match, a pre-base commit ignored, no ref, no intent, and a non-ff records history.
Add the CLI flag, dispatch and display renderer (text and JSON), exiting 2 on a finding.
Add the binary tests for help, conflicts and the no-records exit.
Run cargo fmt --all, cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings and cargo test --locked.

risks.risk: The `ci.yml` job cannot be run here, so a mistake in its `if` or fetch step would only show in CI.
risks.mitigation: Copy the structure of the existing `history` and `pr-head` jobs, use `git fetch origin athena/records:athena/records` with persist-credentials left false (the fetch is read-only on a public repo), and mark continue-on-error.

risks.risk: On the first run the records branch may not exist on origin, so the fetch step fails and the job is red.
risks.mitigation: The job is non-blocking. The command also reports a missing ref as an explicit finding rather than a crash.

risks.risk: Two intents may match one commit, or a landing may cite a missing intent.
risks.mitigation: A landing whose intent is missing or mismatched makes that commit a finding. Test it.

risks.risk: Timestamps: an intent created in the future compared with now.
risks.mitigation: Treat now earlier than created_at + 15m as pending; test the boundary.

demonstrations.method: Unit test in attribution.rs. Build a temp repo with a base commit and a squash commit (a one-parent commit whose tree is the head tree). Write the landing-intent (expected_base = base, head_tree = squash tree) and a landing (host_commit = squash, intent = intent id) to athena/records with RecordsWriter. Run the check at a time just after the landing.
demonstrations.observes: The report has no findings and the squash is counted as attributed.
demonstrations.fails_without: If the landing/intent match logic is missing or wrong (for example the tree or expected base compared wrongly), the squash is flagged and the test fails.

demonstrations.method: Unit test. Add a second main commit with no intent and no landing, then run the check.
demonstrations.observes: The report fails and its Unattributed finding contains that commit's full sha; the rendered text also names it.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the unattributed rule the commit would pass silently and the assertion on the finding fails.

demonstrations.method: Unit test. Main commit with a matching intent and no landing. Run at intent.created_at + 14 minutes, then at + 16 minutes, and also at exactly +15 minutes.
demonstrations.observes: At +14 and +15 minutes there are no findings and the commit is listed as pending. At +16 minutes the report has a finding for the commit naming the expired intent.
demonstrations.fails_without: With no pending window the +14 case fails; with no expiry the +16 case passes and the test fails.

demonstrations.method: Unit test in attribution.rs, plus a unit test of `audit_history` in records_branch.rs. Create a records history with a later commit built with `commit_tree` on a different or missing parent chain (a second root), and another that drops a prior file. Run the check.
demonstrations.observes: The report has a records-history finding naming the offending records commit. A normally written branch (including a commit with an extra parent) has none.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the audit, the rewritten history yields no finding and the test fails.

demonstrations.method: Binary tests in crates/athena-cli/tests/binary.rs run the real binary with `check --help`. A second test runs `check --attribution --history` and `check --attribution --pr-head a b`.
demonstrations.observes: The help lists `--attribution`. Through cargo test -p athena-cli --test binary, the combined invocations exit non-zero with a clap conflict message on stderr, and `--attribution` alone in a repo without athena/records exits 2 with a finding.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without conflicts_with_all, the combinations would be accepted and the test fails.

demonstrations.method: Read the code and `git diff`. Confirm the module and function doc comments cite records-history.md §5.2, §6, §10 and D111, and the module doc states records-only and the base bound. Confirm no use of trailers, `Change::trailers`, `interpret-trailers` or `log_grep` in attribution.rs. The test that a pre-base commit is not judged (an unrecorded commit before the intent's expected_base) must pass.
demonstrations.observes: The doc comments are present, there are no trailer calls, and the pre-base-commit test shows no finding for it.

demonstrations.method: Read the workflow diff. The `attribution` job has continue-on-error: true and `if: github.event_name == 'push' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' || github.event_name == 'schedule'`. It uses checkout at fetch-depth 0 with the same SHA pin as the other jobs. A step runs `git fetch origin athena/records:athena/records` before the `athena check --attribution` step (preceded by `./setup.sh --ci`). The comment says it is not a required check. The command reads refs/heads/athena/records, then falls back to refs/remotes/origin/athena/records.
demonstrations.observes: All of the listed properties appear in the diff, and the `uses:` lines carry full 40-hex SHAs identical to existing ones.
No warnings. `cargo fmt --check` reports no diff and `cargo test` passes across the workspace.

open_questions: Whether history.rs needs a change at all: the plan leaves it untouched unless the producer wants to share the first-parent helper.
